summary: Build practical internal controls skills for finance, NGO, and public-sector audits. Create matrices, test controls, and monitor exceptions. Enrol today.
lede: Internal controls design and testing helps finance, grants, programme and audit professionals turn risks into documented safeguards and verifiable evidence. Participants learn to map financial and programme risks to preventive and detective controls, assess segregation-of-duties conflicts, and test whether controls operate as intended. They also practise recording exceptions, assigning corrective actions, and presenting results through workpapers and monitoring dashboards.
audienceIntro: This internal controls training suits professionals who design, operate, review, or report on safeguards across finance, grants, programmes, and public accountability functions. It is particularly relevant when you need to strengthen control evidence without assuming a large technology budget or a fully mature assurance function.
prerequisites: You should have working exposure to finance, grants, programme delivery, internal audit, compliance, or public-sector accounting processes. No coding or programming is required. You should bring examples of non-confidential process maps, approval workflows, audit findings, or control registers if available. Advanced digital monitoring concepts receive conceptual and operational treatment, while spreadsheet-based dashboard exercises provide the main hands-on technology practice.
